macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise ahead of Fed decision and major tech earnings
items.summary: U.S. equities advanced for a second session, led by technology shares and renewed optimism around artificial-intelligence spending. Investors were awaiting the Federal Reserve’s policy decision and earnings reports from Alphabet and Microsoft after the close.[1][3]

items.title: Fed decision becomes central market catalyst
items.summary: The Federal Reserve was scheduled to announce its interest-rate decision at 2 p.m. ET, with markets expecting rates to remain unchanged after a September increase. Investors were also assessing the possibility of another hike at the Fed’s December meeting.[3][4]

items.title: Tech futures edge higher while Treasury yields rise
items.summary: Ahead of the Fed decision, Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.5% and S&P 500 futures about 0.1%, while Dow futures were slightly lower. Treasury yields moved higher as investors prepared for monetary-policy guidance and major earnings.[3][7]

items.title: Alphabet and Microsoft earnings in focus
items.summary: Alphabet and Microsoft were scheduled to report quarterly results after the U.S. market close, making their updates a major test of whether AI investment is translating into sufficient revenue and profits.[3][8]

items.title: SK Hynix reports sharp profit surge on AI memory demand
items.summary: SK Hynix reported third-quarter operating profit of 83.33 trillion won, up 632% year over year, with revenue rising 328% to a record 104.615 trillion won. The company also outlined plans to return 100 trillion won to shareholders this year, reinforcing enthusiasm for semiconductor and AI-related stocks.[4]

items.title: Bank of Japan expected to hold rates at 1.25%
items.summary: Markets largely expected the Bank of Japan to leave its policy rate at 1.25%, shifting attention to Governor Kazuo Ueda’s guidance on the timing of a possible future rate hike.[1][7]

items.title: New Zealand dollar falls after central bank holds rates
items.summary: The New Zealand dollar fell more than 1% after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand unexpectedly left its policy rate unchanged, contrary to market expectations.[8]

items.title: October U.S. consumer confidence rebounds
items.summary: The Conference Board’s consumer-confidence index rose to 91.7 in October from 84.2 in September, exceeding economists’ expectations of 81.[5]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rises above $84,000 as major tokens gain
items.summary: Bitcoin traded above $84,000, up about 1.17% over 24 hours. Several large-cap tokens also advanced, while short liquidations exceeded long liquidations on major exchanges.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds as spot ETF inflows accelerate
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 1.3% to above $82,700 as broader risk appetite improved. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs reportedly attracted $527 million in inflows, the strongest daily inflow since September 22.

items.title: Zcash jumps 11% ahead of NU7 upgrade
items.summary: Zcash gained roughly 11% to about $1,260 after developers set the NU7 mainnet activation for block 3,543,405, expected around November 5.

items.title: Binance applies for Brazilian crypto license
items.summary: Binance submitted an application for a virtual-asset service-provider license in Brazil before the October 30 deadline. Its Brazilian unit also restricted eight services and delisted 22 tokens locally.

items.title: Ripple receives final approval for U.S. trust bank
items.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency approved Ripple National Trust Bank, which is expected to custody assets supporting RLUSD and hold crypto for businesses. The bank will not take deposits or make loans.

items.title: Aviva launches tokenized money-market fund share class on XRP Ledger
items.summary: Aviva Investors and Ripple launched a tokenized share class of the firm’s sterling liquidity fund on the XRP Ledger, with Aviva investing £50 million.

items.title: Liquid Network redemption freeze continues after exploit
items.summary: Liquid Network’s LBTC-to-Bitcoin redemptions remain suspended 35 days after an Elements software exploit. The attacker reportedly still holds about 598.5 BTC, valued near $49.7 million.

items.title: South Korea may delay cryptocurrency capital-gains tax
items.summary: South Korea’s presidential office is reportedly considering postponing the planned 22% cryptocurrency-gains tax, scheduled to begin in January 2027, until 2029.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google DeepMind previews Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind previewed Genie 4, a world model designed to generate more realistic interactive 3D environments with native real-time audio. The model is initially available to trusted testers and can reportedly maintain scene consistency for up to two minutes.

items.title: Nvidia and Meta expand Muse AI partnership
items.summary: Nvidia and Meta announced an expanded collaboration on Meta’s Muse family of models, including infrastructure and performance improvements. Nvidia also plans to invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering.

items.title: Oracle to offer Google TPU infrastructure
items.summary: Oracle and Google announced that Google’s tensor processing units will become available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, extending access to Google-designed AI accelerators beyond Google’s own cloud.

items.title: Anthropic expands government Claude partnership
items.summary: Anthropic announced an expanded agreement with the U.S. General Services Administration that provides government partners with a 40% discount on Claude, potentially reducing public-sector AI costs by about $1 billion.

items.title: Anthropic reports early drug-development collaborations
items.summary: Anthropic described early work with six drug-development partners and announced its acquisition of Mithril, a small company focused on muscular dystrophy research, highlighting growing use of AI in biomedical discovery.

items.title: OpenAI announces scientific research claims
items.summary: OpenAI publicized claimed advances in mathematics, computer science, and physics, including results that experts are expected to independently evaluate. The announcements also included a revised approach to communicating research findings.

items.title: Machenta raises $40 million for robot-learning model
items.summary: London-based Machenta raised a $40 million seed round to develop an AI model intended to teach robots new physical tasks after observing a demonstration once, reflecting continued investment in embodied and robotic AI.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero set for October 29 release
items.summary: S-Game’s action RPG Phantom Blade Zero is scheduled to launch on PC and PlayStation 5 on October 29.

items.title: U.S. game spending declined 1% in September
items.summary: Circana reported that U.S. video game spending fell 1% year over year in September. Marvel’s Wolverine led monthly full-game dollar sales, while NBA 2K27 became 2026’s best-selling game year to date.

items.title: Rockstar workers to vote on union recognition
items.summary: Rockstar Games employees are expected to vote in November on whether the company should recognize the Rockstar Game Workers Union, potentially creating the largest recognized union in the UK games industry.

items.title: Warhorse Studios confirms cyberattack
items.summary: Kingdom Come: Deliverance developer Warhorse Studios confirmed unauthorized access to its systems and data and said it is investigating the incident.

items.title: Pocketpair open to bringing Palworld to Switch 2
items.summary: Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe said the studio would welcome discussions about releasing Palworld on Nintendo’s Switch 2.

items.title: Phasmophobia’s Resonance update delayed to late November
items.summary: Kinetic Games plans to release Phasmophobia’s Resonance update in late November 2026, adding Unity 6 improvements, new ghost-interaction features, and Xbox Play Anywhere support.

items.title: KartBoard Dash announces competitive mode and console ports
items.summary: Following its PC, Android, and iOS launch, KartBoard Dash announced a Championship Mode and plans to release the arcade racer on PlayStation 5, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch.

items.title: Pokémon Unite service-ending announcement draws fan reaction
items.summary: Japanese media reported that Pokémon Unite will end service, prompting strong reactions from players; the available report does not specify the shutdown date.
